name: Twenty One Pilots

eras.name: early
eras.notes: Looser, more eclectic, piano-driven. Lyrically raw.

eras.name: breakthrough
eras.notes: More polished production, bigger choruses. 'Blurryface' character introduced.

eras.name: lore
eras.notes: Dense, dark, fully committed to mythology. Yellow imagery dominant.

eras.name: pandemic-pivot
eras.notes: Brighter, more pop-leaning surface; the mythology is hidden underneath.

eras.name: return-to-source
eras.notes: Closes the mythological arc; blends Trench-era darkness with Scaled and Icy brightness.

themes: mental health (anxiety, depression, dissociation, suicidal ideation)
identity (who am I vs. who I present as)
fear of failure / fear of obscurity
the relationship between artist and listener

symbols.meaning: bandit identity, hope; especially Trench/Clancy era
the rebel faction in the Dema mythology

symbols.symbol: voices in the head / two minds
symbols.meaning: tied to the mythology and to mental health themes

instrumentation_present: bass synth (often the melodic lead low end)
tom-heavy drums with a distinctive snare crack
instrumentation_absent: electric guitar (notably sparse across much of the catalog; deliberate when it appears)
rhetorical_habits: conditional and questioning constructions ('if I... would I...')
self-referential meta-lines about the writing/performing itself
structural_tendencies: multiple hooks rather than one repeated chorus
occasional time-signature and tempo changes within a song
mythology_notes: The Dema/Clancy mythology spans Blurryface, Trench, Scaled and Icy, and Clancy: characters (Clancy, Nico, the Bishops, the bandits), places (Dema, Trench), and an ongoing narrative. Many songs work both as standalone emotional pieces and as plot points in this larger story. Generated lyrics that gesture at this mythology should not contradict established canon.
data_sources_note: See docs/case-studies/twenty-one-pilots.md for the full case study and docs/research/legal-and-ethics.md before adding real corpus material to data/artists/top/corpus/.
